Listen to this article Share A faction of youth supporters in the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has withdrawn its backing for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid, exposing a rift in the party’s northern base. Advertisement Advertisement The Anti-Tinubu APC Northern Youths Forum, which claims to draw members from Nigeria’s 19 northern states, announced the decision at a news conference at the Kano Press Centre on Saturday. However, the group said it remains committed to the APC. It will continue to campaign for the party’s governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and state assembly candidates across northern Nigeria. Security and economic grievances Forum secretary Umar Chanji, who spoke on behalf of chairman Mustapha Tinubu and other leaders, said the administration had failed to meet its promises on security, education, healthcare and economic development. Chanji said protecting lives and property—the core duty of government—had grown increasingly difficult across northern Nigeria as attacks by terrorists and other criminal groups persisted. He listed Katsina, Sokoto, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Nasarawa, Benue, Kaduna, Kebbi, Bauchi, Taraba, Kwara and Kogi states, alongside the Federal Capital Territory, as areas hit by ongoing insecurity. Advertisement According to Chanji, the violence has destroyed communities, displaced thousands of residents and disrupted farming and other economic activities, deepening financial strain on households. The group also faulted the federal government’s economic policies, specifically the removal of petrol subsidies and new taxes. It said these measures increased costs for ordinary Nigerians without improving living standards. The forum also questioned the rollout of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) as an alternative fuel and delays in rehabilitating state-owned refineries. Advertisement Healthcare, education and party appointments On education, the group said insecurity continued to keep children out of school in several northern communities, while displacement had forced families to abandon their homes and farms. Advertisement Advertisement It also criticised the state of public healthcare, alleging that underfunded medical facilities and limited state support exposed vulnerable citizens to preventable deaths. Additionally, the forum accused unnamed political appointees of prioritising personal and family interests over public welfare. The forum’s stance also reflects discontent over political patronage. Chanji alleged that grassroots youths who mobilised for the APC during the 2023 presidential election had been sidelined in political appointments in favour of individuals with close ties to government officials. He described the trend as political marginalisation. Implications for 2027 The development adds a new layer to the APC’s political calculations ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party relies heavily on northern Nigeria to consolidate its support base and secure a presidential victory. While the forum did not verify its membership size or its ability to sway voters across the 19 northern states, its stance signals pockets of discontent among grassroots supporters. By backing other APC candidates while rejecting Tinubu, the group is attempting to separate party loyalty from support for the president’s second term. Chanji urged APC members and northern youths to reconsider backing Tinubu’s re-election, insisting the forum’s decision was driven by the administration’s failure to meet public expectations.
